main_text.p: Bismuthum eft corpus minerale, livedinis albicantis, durum, fragile, cõstans mercurio albo, terreo, sulphureq; tali & arsenico, omnibus volaticis & impuris, medium inter Plumbi genera & Antimonium.Bismuthum,

Antimonium eft corpus minerale, durum, terrestre, fragile, constans ex sulphure & arsenico turbido, & hydrargyro magis terreo, omnibus tamen volatilibus magis quàm bismuthum, vitiatis quadam terrea minerali vitrea.Antimonium,
Itaq; halitum edit fœtidû plurimumque, qui quia est mercurialis majore ex parte, minore sulphureus & arsenicalis, niveus est, sublataq; parte spirituosiore ob sulphur in rubeā mutatur tinsturam.
Sulphur est succus mineralis pinguis, fœtorem acrem & pungentem emittens, habens partem subtilem, inflammatilé, partem crassam, terream, fixam, intermistam succo chalcantoso.Sulphur,
Itaque ob illam inflammatur facilè, ob hanc figitur, ut nullis ignibus possit incendi.
Metallorum Pater dicitur, cum accedit spiritus metallicus, seminali metallo-rum

page.notes: Right margin notes transcribed as catchwords of the entries: "Bismuthum", "Antimonium", "Sulphur". Long s rendered as plain s. The last line ends with a hyphenated word continuing as "rum" on the bottom line, which is the printed running word at the foot of the column and is kept as printed. Faint show-through of the reverse page is ignored.
